questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To study in an internationally recognised university, with an interesting program and new topics and courses; To have a cheap and easy to find accomodation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Uppsala is a great place to study, with students and university buildings all around the town. I think it would have been nice to know beforehand that SLU is a bit outside of the city. It means that you have to choose to have a room either close to the city or close to SLU. However, it's great to bike around and most of the way is flat and pretty. In Uppsala center, there are a lot of student groups and activities, which is very unique to Uppsala and makes it super easy to meet new people and start new hobbies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: SLU has an agreement with several housing buildings around Uppsala, which made it super easy to arrive and move in directly. The only thing is that you need to arrive during a working day and not in the evening. The course information were sent to me both trough my regular email and on canvas. You need to set up your SLU email beforehand but you just need to video call someone from the IT department and then you can access it very easily.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I could drop by the building office to get my key and drop my suitcases directly after my arrival in Uppsala. We also had a meeting with Ulf, who is the responsible for the EnvEuro students, a bit later after we all arrived. It was nice to meet all the students and then we could keep in touch and meet eachothers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Corridor rooms are available right next to the campus (SUSBO). The price is ok (4600 SEK) but international students who stay in those rooms through SLU pay a bit more because of the furnitures. If you apply for a room without the SLU, they the room is not furnished but you have 700 SEK less to pay each month.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In that housing place (SUBSO), there is 1 kitchen shared with 8 people. In general, it is not so common to share meals with your roommates there, so everyone cooks when they are hungry and you don't have big community meals all together. There are usually common dishes to share but everyone has their own too. You can use the common one, as an international student. Everyone has 1 towel so bring your own or find one at a second hand shop when you arrive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of international students but usually they are spread in different corridors. I think if you apply on time you could get a room without going through the SLU and thus you would pay a bit less, but have no furnitures. The thing is that you don't get to choose who you live with or what it is gonna be like, but when the weather is nice you can sit outside with other friends or invite other students for lunch. The campus is really 2 minutes away by bike so you can also save a lot of time in the morning, and money because you can come back and eat lunch at home rather than paying for a meal on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The rental contract with SUSBO through SLU is from the 1st of August till the 15th of August on the next year, or the 15th of June. It is good to know that the courses usually end early June. I think that the notice period is only one month when you rent the room through SLU, while it is 3months when you rent the room direclty from SUSBO.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: From what I remembered, I think it was quite easy. I don't ramember any difficult procedure.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will receive a student number by email called the "T number". Then on "Ladok" you need to register for the courses you chose. I think you register for the whole semester at once. It is a bit tricky to understand because you have to register for your second choices as well, in case you are not accepted in the courses you want. In case you are interested for the internship, then you have to notify the international team by email because the "course" does not appear on Ladok.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were very reactive by email and super ready to help in case you have any question.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. If not, you automatically get your second choices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask questions by email if you are lost. Everyone is very helpful. Make sure your total number of ETCS is correct.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt like the academic program was not sufficiently deep compared to my bachelor program in Belgium. But I think most of the students I met from other countries tend to say that the courses were more chill and required less work and study than in their home countries (Belgium, Germany, Austria, Netherlands, ...)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I chose started back to basics witch made it super nice to follow because everyone was on the same level and could understand the rest of the course super easily. However, for people who are super advanced in some topics, they might get a bit bored because most of the courses don't go too deep into one particular topic. It depends on which course you choose for sure, but for 7.5 or 15 ECTS I would have expected more work and more interesting things.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is quite similar. The teachers are available to answer your questions. They start back from the start with most of the topics and they were usually very good at teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Soil water processes in agroecosystems - MV0216
Land use and watershed management to reduce eutrophication - MV0217
Geographic information systems for environmental and natural science studies - TE0017

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master thesis in Environmental science, A2E - EX0897

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
"Soil water processes in agroecosystems" was a nice course to learn the basics of working with a soil/water model. The teacher is super nice and helpful. We had a few theoric courses and then mostly "labs" where we met in a computer room and had exercises with "Stella" the model used. We usually finished earlier than scheduled.
"Land use and watershed management to reduce eutrophication" is a course about water in agriculture and we had a few field trips. However, the course is in November so the weather was already super cold and it's not the best time to stay outside. The teacher is a great woman but she had a bit too much expectations with the course as it used to be a 15 ECTS course and it has been reduced to 7.5. There is quite a lot of work and courses. 
"GIS for environmental and natural science studies" was a beginners' course on GIS, that was given fully online even without covid restriction in Sweden. It was nice beacuse we could schedule our work as we wanted, as the courses were prerecorded and the exercises you could do whenever you wanted. The course was super usefull! You even get a certificate in the end, with your level in GIS. The teacher is however hard to understand, especiallyy because the GIS theory is quite hard to get.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay around 150 DKK each time you use the train to and from the airport! Plus the train price. That makes it super expensive! You can take a bus but it takes longer and is still quite expensive. Transportation is expensive in Sweden but you can buy a second hand bike easily and bike around in Uppsala.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is more or less as expensive as in Denmark. Transportation is expensive so sometimes renting a car for the weekend is the cheapest option. You also have GoMore to rent people's car.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were still in a covid period.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think there were sports and student commities at SLU but I don't know about it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Uppsala is full of student nations, which used to be "home" for students all around Sweden. There is Stockholm nation, Gotland nation, Kalmar nation etc. Each nation has a pub that serves food and drinks. They also have specific activities such as sports, flea markets, yoga, boardgames and a lot of other things. You have to pay around 220 DKK as a membership, and then you are allowed to enter any nation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of nature reserve around. Download the app "Natuurkartan" and check on which walks you can do around Uppsala. This app works for all Sweden and shows where you can ice skate on lakes in winter, where you have mountain bike tracks, walking path, fire places (usually with chopped wood available), free access huts to spend the night in, etc. Great if you want to spend time outside and in the nature. Otherwise I would recommend to go in some of the national parks around Sweden. Abikso is great for a few days but has no network. Stockholm is also nice to go to before Christmas. Sigtuna has a great Christmas Market too.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was ok. The hardest thing was that everyone would cook for themselves in the corridor so that we would never really have dinners together. I thing it would be the nicest thing as an exchange student when you arrive. But it also depends on who you live with.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Join a nation :)
And get out of your comfort zone: everyone is looking for new friends!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing that I can think of.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoors loving and caring. The fact that people go for barbecues in fireplaces in winter because there is chopped wood available.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Uppsala is a small city and it can feel a bit quiet when you get there, but try to enjoy 
- The student life!
- The outdoors (the nature is so close)
- Find the Sweeds that want to hang out with international: they have so much to share on their culture and some of them are not as shy as you might think.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a direct train connexion from Copenhagen to Stockholm with SJ. Super easy ! If you want cheaper fares, there are student prices, and other train companies such as Snalltaget. That connexion requires a swith in Malmö as well. 
You should also get a "mecenat" card, which is gonna be your student card. It is shown on an app and gives access to a lot of discounts, from which one can be used with Snalltaget.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to know another culture and enjoy my exchange because I did not have to work too hard for uni. The proximity with nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The winter. The sun goes down so early and you lack energy and motivation to go out or to go on trips.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
